items.title: [rucio] rucio has an Authorization Bypass on REST API endpoint for signing URLs
items.summary: SummaryThe /credentials/signurl endpoint decides authorization from the client-supplied X-Rucio-Account HTTP header instead of the authenticated token's account. Any client holding any valid auth token (even a low-privilege account they legitimately own) can send X-Rucio-Account: root to pass the root-only permission check and have the Rucio server mint a presigned read / write / delete URL for an arbitrary object, signed with the RSE's stored S3 / GCS / Swift credentials.DetailsSignURL.get() takes the authorization principal from a request header andnever uses the token-authenticated identity:# lib/rucio/web/rest/flaskapi/v1/credentials.pyaccount = request.headers.get('X-Rucio-Account', default=None)     # L165  (attacker-controlled)...result = get_signed_url(account, rse=rse, service=service,         # L194                        operation=operation, url=url, lifetime=lifetime, vo=vo)The gateway then uses that header value as the issuer for the permission check:# lib/rucio/gateway/credential.pyauth_result = permission.has_permission(issuer=account, vo=vo,     # L57                                        action='get_signed_url', kwargs=kwargs, ...)and the permission function is root-only:# lib/rucio/core/permission/generic.pydef perm_get_signed_url(issuer, kwargs, session):    return _is_root(issuer)        # _is_root(x) -> x.external == 'root'InternalAccount('root', vo).external == 'root' unconditionally, so the gate passes whenever the header is root. The endpoint is on AuthenticatedBlueprint, whose before_request hook validates the token and sets request.environ['issuer'] from the token — but nothing ever compares X-Rucio-Account to it:# lib/rucio/web/rest/flaskapi/v1/common.py  (request_auth_env)flask.request.environ['issuer'] = auth.get('account')             # L168  (the real account; unused by SignURL)This is anomalous: every other authenticated handler derives the account from request.environ['issuer']; credentials.py is the only one that trusts the header. Additionally, core.credential.get_signed_url never checks that the supplied url's host/bucket belongs to the target RSE, so even a legitimate root caller gets an arbitrary-object signing oracle. In multi-VO the VO is also read from the X-Rucio-VO header, allowing cross-tenant targeting.Proof of conceptRequest (any valid token + spoofed account):GET /credentials/signurl?rse=<cloudRSE>&svc=s3&op=delete&url=https://victim-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/important/dataset.root HTTP/1.1X-Rucio-Auth-Token: <any valid token, even a low-privilege account>X-Rucio-Account: rootAccept: application/octet-streamResponse: 200 OK with a presigned DELETE URL the attacker replays directly against the storage backend.ImpactA low-privilege Rucio user can read, overwrite, and delete arbitrary objects on any cloud-backed (S3/GCS/Swift) RSE using the server's stored credentials — enabling data exfiltration, tampering, and destruction, and cross-tenant access in multi-VO deployments.CreditReported by seankohjs. Found via static analysis + manual verification.Referenceshttps://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-5j9r-fx4x-rpvghttps://github.com/rucio/rucio/commit/64c0e6a6a93ae88427ff3b7d77532ce08c8a69echttps://github.com/rucio/rucio/commit/8bdc38994a8766658d0314d36afc104c9242c96fhttps://github.com/rucio/rucio/commit/8d9ba31514e6f5dca32b8c1db4738582cb37ec3ahttps://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/35.9.0https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/38.6.0https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/41.0.0rc1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5j9r-fx4x-rpvg
